assertion_audit.fails_if: The positive controls contain no real duties, invalidating an empty-result parity or absence claim.
The input hold is not entered or the case does not release its worker; these validate the fixture, not product behavior.
Restoring the global report lock prevents READY finishing before the ten-second bound while SLOW holds pruning; the base negative control records this failure.
The independently derived cold payload differs from the completed stored answer, including missing or changed duties.
Removing pending publication loses retained duties or the stale age, timestamp, or reason; the base negative control loses the stale marker.
The stale key and the identity in the current stored row differ; both moving together does not fail, so this checks internal consistency only (finding recorded).
Export is missing/different, unfinished SLOW is no longer in flight, completed READY is absent or wrongly heartbeat-stale, or the hold was released before the independent export.

Workers leak, completed rows remain stale or empty, or an unchanged supplied payload moves identity/changed_at; supplying the previous payload deliberately creates an unchanged derivation and does not make the independent stored stamp assertions tautological.
An unread first refresh manufactures a document, age, export, or station answer; the independently nonempty READY control establishes the reader can see completed work.
Publishing again before the refresh floor rewrites the stored row or export despite no change.
No added assertion fails when a retained stale answer is presented by the production hook as current; no reader-time stale-age advance is asserted.

findings.text: blocking: the retained answer is marked only inside its payload, whereas obligation_snapshot.py:708-719 derives the reader's stale flag solely from heartbeat age and coordinator_obligations.py:1492-1550 renders a fresh-heartbeat answer with no retained-answer warning; format_checklist at line 895 ignores the payload stale marker, so a project still reading is presented as current rather than stale with its age as the goal requires.

non-blocking: the stale key is compared with stored_identity of the current output row rather than the captured previous_row, so rewriting both identity and stale key together preserves this assertion despite losing the last answer's key; compare against the pre-refresh identity in the source node's repair.
